hook: Read an essay on forgetting in the digital age and catch what the author concedes, what he rejects and how he redefines.
intro: An essay of about 430 words on forgetting in the age of digital storage. It follows the classic essay line: a striking opening („Wir leben im Zeitalter der totalen Speicherung.“), a concession („Man mag das zunächst für einen Gewinn halten, und in mancher Hinsicht ist es einer“), the hinge („Doch gerade darin liegt eine unterschätzte Gefahr.“), the redefinition of the key concept („Das Vergessen ist jedoch keine bloße Schwäche des Gedächtnisses, sondern vielmehr eine seiner wichtigsten Leistungen.“), an example, a limitation of the author’s own claim („Nichts davon ist ein Plädoyer für das Verdrängen.“) and a conclusion that reinterprets the „Recht auf Vergessen“. The questions ask about stance and argument, not facts: what the author concedes, what he rejects, and how he redefines.
tips[0].title: Stance in the modifiers
tips[0].text: The author’s evaluation sits in small words: bloße (only / mere – he denies that it is only that), unterschätzte (others rate it too low), gerade (precisely there, against expectation), notorisch, gleichgültig. Questions about the author’s view are answered by these modifiers, not by the nouns.
tips[0].check.why: bloße denies the 'only': the author says it is not just a formality but something more.
tips[1].title: Redefinition: X ist nicht …, sondern vielmehr …
tips[1].text: The essayist’s core move: name the usual reading of a concept, deny it, and supply his own. The text does this twice – for forgetting and for the right to be forgotten. The rejected reading often turns up as a distractor, so check which half of the sentence an option paraphrases.
tips[1].trap: The first half of a nicht …, sondern … sentence is the view the author rejects. An option that paraphrases it is wrong, however faithfully it quotes the text.
tips[1].check.why: The first half of a nicht …, sondern vielmehr … sentence is the rejected view; the author’s own is after sondern.
tips[2].title: Concession → hinge → limitation → conclusion
tips[2].text: Mark the moves: the concession (mag … halten, in mancher Hinsicht), the hinge (Doch gerade darin), the author’s self-limitation (Nichts davon ist …) and the closing reinterpretation (Vielleicht ist … am Ende …). The self-limitation matters: it tells you what the author does NOT claim.
tips[2].check.why: Nichts davon ist … tells you what the author does not claim: it is his self-limitation.
tips[2].visual.moves[0].label: Concession
tips[2].visual.moves[1].label: Hinge
tips[2].visual.moves[2].label: Limitation
tips[2].visual.moves[3].label: Redefinition
remember[0]: Concession (mag … halten, in mancher Hinsicht) → Doch gerade darin → the author’s own view.
remember[1]: nicht …, sondern vielmehr …: the first half is rejected, the second half is the author’s definition.
remember[2]: bloße, unterschätzte, gerade: stance lives in the modifiers.
remember[3]: Nichts davon ist …: the author limits his own claim – options that go beyond it are traps.
exam: Tracking an essayist’s stance is a core C2 reading skill in the exam — and on every feature page and opinion column you read.

tips[0].check.options[0]: It is more than a mere formality.
tips[0].check.answer: It is more than a mere formality.
